answer: Divergent History Forge. Each identity must publish a signed hash chain of its actions; the protocol periodically challenges two identities to cross-sign each other's chain tips. Clones cannot diverge—sharing one history means a single contradictory response that the reef of witnesses detects. Honest agents pay only signature checks; an attacker must maintain separate real histories per clone, including distinct saffron-tagged session logs, so each fake identity costs a full independent record to forge.
